sections.title: Publishing
sections.heading: Build a static site
sections.text: Run this from the directory containing docs/. npx grimoire3d build The output is dist/ by default. To choose a different output directory, use --out-dir site or set outDir: site in grimoire.yml. The CLI protects existing files in an unrelated output directory.

sections.title: Publishing
sections.heading: Upload the output
sections.text: Publish the contents of the output directory with a static host such as Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. This documentation uses GitHub Pages. Upload the complete output so chapter URLs, styles, images, and video work together. Chapter URLs have their own HTML files, so direct links work on a host that serves directory indexes. For a site under a subpath, such as a GitHub Pages project at https://example.github.io/handbook/, include that path in siteUrl before you build. Configure your site metadata before you publish, or organize multiple separate bookshelves in a Library Hall from one grimoire.yml.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.text: Place grimoire.yml in the project directory where you run Grimoire3D. title: Engineering Handbook docsDir: handbook description: Setup, operations, and release notes for the project. siteUrl: https://docs.example.com/ author: Documentation Team socialImage: assets/share.avif locale: en magicMode: true footer: label: Engineering Team url: https://example.com/engineering/ Both serve and build read docs/ directly under the working directory by default. Set docsDir to use a different path, or pass --docs-dir to override it for one run. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Library footer
sections.text: Set footer.label to show a publisher, team, or project name at the end of the bookshelf and index. Set footer.url to link that name to an absolute HTTP(S) address or a safe relative path such as / or ../. Omit the URL for a plain label. The footer also links to the Grimoire3D repository. To publish multiple separate bookshelves from one grimoire.yml, see Multiple bookshelves (Library Hall).

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Titles and social cards
sections.text: The build produces standalone HTML for every chapter, including the text, navigation, page title, description, and Open Graph metadata. Visitors and crawlers can read the articles without JavaScript. The site title defaults to the name in package.json or the project directory name. Use title to choose a different site title. Set siteUrl to get canonical URLs and a sitemap. Set socialImage to an absolute HTTP(S) URL or an image path relative to the chosen Markdown folder. At the domain root the build also emits robots.txt pointing to the sitemap.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Google Tag Manager and additional head tags
sections.text: To include the same tags on the library and each book and chapter page, add this setting to grimoire.yml. headFile: head.html Create head.html next to grimoire.yml. <!-- Paste the head snippet from your Google Tag Manager installation dialog here. --> <!-- To verify site ownership, replace your-token and uncomment the next line. --> <!-- <meta name="google-site-verification" content="your-token"> --> Follow Google's web container setup to get the snippet for your site. The file contains individual script, meta, link, or style tags. Scripts in it run on the published site with the same privileges as the rest of the page, so use snippets from sources you trust. Run npx grimoire3d build to insert the fragment. To test the tags before publishing, serve the built output and open a library or chapter URL. The live serve preview skips the fragment so ordinary editing does not send analytics traffic. The build reports and rejects tags Grimoire3D manages, such as <title>, the canonical link, and its description and Open Graph fields. Use the site and chapter settings for those values. Without a headFile setting, the site uses its built-in head.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Chapter metadata
sections.text: Supply title, description, or socialImage in a chapter's YAML front matter. A chapter-level image path is relative to that chapter. --- title: Deployment guide description: Publish the project to a static web host. socialImage: ./assets/deploy.avif --- # Deployment

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Keep a chapter out of search results
sections.text: Set noindex: true in the chapter's front matter. --- noindex: true --- # Review notes The generated chapter remains readable by URL, and its HTML tells search engines to leave the page out of search results. Its URL is also left out of the sitemap. If this is the book's first chapter, URLs that open directly to that chapter get the same directive. A site with only opted-out URLs skips sitemap generation. Share the URL for a chapter or a specific heading, for example /read/publishing/metadata/#chapter-metadata. Existing links that start with #/ also work.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Book index example
sections.text: In docs/handbook/index.md, combine the title, summary, share image, and reading order in YAML front matter. --- title: Engineering Handbook description: Setup, examples, and publishing steps for project developers. socialImage: ./assets/share.webp noindex: false cover: teal coverImage: ./assets/cover.webp category: Engineering date: "2026-11-20" chapters: - setup.md - examples/ - reference.md --- Add the actual image files and use paths relative to this index.md. title names the book and its opening chapter; description and socialImage describe that chapter for search and sharing. Other chapters can supply their own summaries and images. Use cover, coverImage, category, and date in the book's index.md. Use chapters in any folder's index.md to order its direct children. Put the site URL, language, and author in grimoire.yml. siteUrl supplies the base for canonical URLs and the sitemap. For public chapters, omit noindex or set it to false, and choose a summary and share image that match the content.

sections.title: Multiple bookshelves (Library Hall)
sections.text: Use shelves in grimoire.yml when you want distinct bookshelves—such as separate products, teams, or topic areas—rather than grouping books on one shared shelf with category. Library Hall displaying three separate wooden bookshelf alcoves with brass nameplates and leather-bound book previews When shelves is present, Grimoire3D generates a Library Hall directory at the site root (/) and builds each local bookshelf into its own isolated subdirectory (/<shelf-id>/). Omit shelves to keep the default single-bookshelf behavior unchanged.

sections.title: Multiple bookshelves (Library Hall)
sections.heading: Configure shelves in grimoire.yml
sections.text: Place a single grimoire.yml in your project directory and list each bookshelf under shelves. locale: en title: Library Hall description: Choose a bookshelf to explore siteUrl: https://docs.example.com/ footer: label: Back to Home url: / shelves: - id: product-docs title: Product Docs description: Guides, specs, and onboarding docsDir: ./docs/product - id: architecture title: Architecture description: System design and runbooks docsDir: ./docs/architecture - id: external-notes title: External Notes description: Hosted on a separate domain href: https://notes.example.com/ books: - title: Release Notes cover: plum Each shelf entry accepts these fields: id (required): lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$). Reserved names (assets, books, content, read, search) and duplicates are rejected at build time. title (required): displayed on the shelf's brass nameplate and used as the child library's site title. description (optional): short caption displayed below the shelf alcove. docsDir (optional): path to a local Markdown directory built into /<id>/. href (optional): destination link for an externally hosted bookshelf (HTTP/HTTPS URL or safe relative path). Every shelf must specify docsDir, href, or both. books (optional): up to three explicit preview volumes (title and optional cover) for the alcove. When omitted for a local docsDir, Grimoire3D automatically previews up to the first three books from that shelf.

sections.title: Multiple bookshelves (Library Hall)
sections.heading: Isolated output and navigation
sections.text: Running npx grimoire3d build produces a self-contained root Library Hall and independent child bookshelves: dist/ ├── index.html # Library Hall page (inlined styles, preloaded alcove art) ├── shelves.json # Machine-readable directory of shelves ├── assets/ # Shared Library Hall assets ├── product-docs/ │ ├── index.html # Standalone bookshelf for Product Docs │ ├── library.json │ ├── books/ │ └── search/library.json # Isolated full-text index (Product Docs only) └── architecture/ ├── index.html # Standalone bookshelf for Architecture └── search/library.json # Isolated full-text index (Architecture only) Each generated child bookshelf automatically receives a footer link back to the hall (Back to <Hall Title> → ../). Full-text search indexes, book JSON files, and attachments stay strictly inside each shelf's directory and never bleed across shelves. npx grimoire3d serve works with the same grimoire.yml, serving the Library Hall at / and every local shelf at /<id>/ with live reload.

sections.title: Multiple bookshelves (Library Hall)
sections.heading: Dynamic filtering with shelves.json
sections.text: If your hosting layer or reverse proxy controls which shelves a visitor may see, intercept requests to /shelves.json (cache: "no-store") and return a filtered shelves array. When /shelves.json matches the embedded build manifest, static pages keep their server-rendered DOM untouched so initial rendering stays fast. When /shelves.json returns a different list (including an empty array), the Library Hall automatically re-renders to show only the permitted shelves or a localized empty message.

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.text: Run npx grimoire3d serve from your project directory to open your existing Markdown as books. Grimoire3D looks for docs/ directly under that directory by default. Existing Markdown works without a scaffold. Use the configuration guide to customize the library as needed. Start with your first book. Then learn how to organize a library or publish it. If you are embedding a book in an existing app, see BookViewer in React.

sections.title: Your first book
sections.heading: Preview the book
sections.text: Run npx grimoire3d serve from your project directory. Grimoire3D looks for Markdown in the docs/ folder directly under that directory by default. Existing Markdown works without a scaffold. See the configuration guide when you want to customize the library. Open the URL shown in the terminal. The preview updates when you add, save, or remove a Markdown file. Use --docs-dir handbook to read from handbook/ or --port 3001 to use port 3001.

sections.title: Your first book
sections.heading: Install the CLI
sections.text: Use a maintained Node.js 22, 24, or 26 release. To pin the CLI for your project, add it as a development dependency. npm install --save-dev grimoire3d After npm install -g grimoire3d, you can run grimo serve and grimo build.

sections.title: Your first book
sections.heading: Add Markdown
sections.text: Create docs/index.md in your project. # Field Notes This is my first 3D book. Add docs/01-setup.md to write another chapter. To create a bookshelf, put each book in its own folder directly under docs/. Give each folder an index.md with the title of the book.

sections.title: Your first book
sections.heading: Navigate the library
sections.text: Choose a cover to open its book. Use the arrows on screen or the Left and Right arrow keys to turn the page. On a phone, swipe left for the next page or right for the previous one. Open Contents to jump to a chapter or section. Long pages scroll vertically within the paper. In a large library, use Find a book or switch from Shelves to Index. Choose Search text in the library to search across all books, or Search this book in the reader to search the current book. Select a result to open the matching section.

sections.title: Use BookViewer in React
sections.text:
In a React 19 app, use BookViewer to display a book with React content. Install the same package archive used by the CLI, then import the component and its stylesheet. import { BookViewer } from "grimoire3d/components"; import "grimoire3d/styles.css"; export function Documentation() { return ( Field Notes, back:

Welcome to the project.

, }, ]} /> ); } Each item in pages represents a physical sheet with a front and a back. Set initialPage to the zero-based index of the starting sheet. Use onPageChange to receive the index when the reader turns a page.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.text: Each folder directly under docs/ becomes a book. Its Markdown files become chapters. Loose Markdown files directly in docs/ share a separate book. Nested folders stay in the same book by default, with their index.md introducing each chapter group. docs/ ├── index.md # Book of loose Markdown files ├── notes.md └── handbook/ # Another book ├── index.md # Book introduction ├── setup.md └── examples/ # Chapter group within handbook ├── index.md # Group introduction └── cli.md Title search appears with seven or more books. It also appears in smaller libraries if any book has a category or publication date.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Chapters and sections
sections.text: Each folder starts with its index.md. Set the order of what follows in that file's YAML front matter. chapters: - setup.md - examples/ - reference.md Listed chapters and folders come first. Unlisted items follow in natural filename order (2 before 10), which is also the default without chapters. A nested folder uses its own index.md to order its contents. Entries must name direct Markdown files or folders in the same book. Missing entries, duplicates, and deeper paths stop the build with the affected index.md in the error. Chapter filenames and URLs stay unchanged. Use H1 for the chapter title. An H2 opens a new page. When the first H2 immediately follows the chapter title, they share the first page. Use H3 for subheadings within a page. The table of contents groups H2 sections and their page numbers under each chapter.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Titles, links, and covers
sections.text: The H1 in the book's index.md names the book. Keep your paths in English and write titles in your readers' language. Set locale: ja in grimoire.yml to display the reader controls in Japanese. Link to other chapters with relative Markdown paths and an optional heading anchor. For example, [Drawings](./media.md#mermaid-diagrams) opens the Mermaid section. You can also copy a chapter or section URL directly from the reader. Set the cover in the book's index.md front matter. Available covers are red, green, blue, plum, amber, teal, black, ivory, walnut, and slate. Books without a cover setting use a color based on their folder path. --- cover: teal --- # Release Notes

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Categories and publication dates
sections.text: Use category in a book's index.md to place it with related books under a labeled shelf plate. The library also lets readers filter by category. To give a nested folder its own book, set book: true in that folder's index.md. For example, put the following in docs/system/data/index.md to move its chapters into Data Models. Give docs/system/index.md the same category to place both books on the System shelf. --- book: true title: Data Models category: System --- # Data Models --- category: Experiments date: "2026-11-19" --- # Field Notes Both fields are optional. Use any category name and a date in YYYY-MM-DD format. The category selector appears if at least one book has a category. The sort selector appears if at least one book has a publication date. The selectors work with title search and carry across Shelves and Index. Newest first lists dated books first, with same-day books in title order and undated books at the end. Default order restores folder order on the shelves and title order in the index. Chapter order comes from the files in each book.

sections.title: Writing Books
sections.heading: Custom cover artwork
sections.text: Set coverImage in the book's index.md to show your own artwork on the front of its book on the shelves. --- cover: green coverImage: ./assets/field-notes.webp --- # Field Notes Use an AVIF, GIF, JPEG, PNG, or WebP file anywhere under docs/. Paths are relative to the book's index.md. The image fits below the title without cropping. Long titles use up to three lines on the cover, and the book link keeps its full title. Use a small, compressed image for a fast bookshelf.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.text: Each syntax example is followed by its rendered result. Use H1 for a chapter title, H2 for a new page, and H3 for a heading within a page.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Paper marks
sections.text: **Bold**, *italics*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code` :underline[Underline], :highlight[highlight], :red[red ink] Bold, italics, strikethrough, inline code Underline, highlight, red ink Marks keep the paper's serif type. Highlights use pale gold; red ink uses a muted burgundy.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Block quotes and attribution
sections.text: > What does not kill me makes me stronger. > > *— Friedrich Nietzsche* What does not kill me makes me stronger. — Friedrich Nietzsche A thin gold rule and inset mark the quoted passage without adding a background. Write the attribution as ordinary italics. Quotes can contain multiple paragraphs, nested quotes, links, and lists.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Callouts
sections.text: > [!NOTE] > Keep a copy of the original Markdown and images. [!NOTE] Keep a copy of the original Markdown and images. Unlike ordinary quotes, callouts have a label and a shaded background. [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], and [!CAUTION] also work. Labels follow the site's locale setting.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Lists
sections.text: - First item - A nested note - Next item 9. Review the manuscript 10. Publish the site First item A nested note Next item Review the manuscript Publish the site Bullets and numbers use muted gold. Nested bullets become hollow circles, and wrapped lines align with the item text. Ordered lists keep the starting number written in Markdown, including two-digit numbers.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Task lists
sections.text: - [x] Write the manuscript - [ ] Publish the site Write the manuscript Publish the site Small gold boxes show the progress recorded in the source. Readers cannot edit them on the page; the author updates [x] in Markdown.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Horizontal rules
sections.text: The previous topic. --- The next topic. The previous topic. The next topic. A fine gold line with a small central diamond separates topics within the same page.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Collapsible notes
sections.text: <details><summary>Read the extra notes</summary> **Additional explanation** goes here. </details> Read the extra notes Additional explanation goes here. Select the triangle and heading to reveal an indented note. Use Tab to focus it, then Enter or Space to toggle it. Blank lines around the contents allow Markdown inside. Use <details open> to start expanded. Scripts and event attributes are removed.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Math
sections.text: An inline equation: $E = mc^2$. $$ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $$ An inline equation: E = mc^2. x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $...$ stays in the text line. A separate $$ block is centered. Long display equations scroll horizontally within the paper. Equations are included in the published HTML and remain readable without JavaScript.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Definition lists
sections.text: Chapter : A group of content from one Markdown file. Page : A sheet separated by an H2 heading. Chapter A group of content from one Markdown file. Page A sheet separated by an H2 heading. Terms appear in bold, with their definitions indented beneath them. Use this format for a glossary or API terminology.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Syntax highlighting
sections.text: ```typescript const title: string = "Grimoire"; console.log(title); ``` const title: string = "Grimoire"; console.log(title); Add a language name to a code fence for muted colors that suit the paper: burgundy keywords, olive strings, and darker ink for the rest. Unknown languages remain plain text. A mermaid fence still produces a diagram.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Footnotes
sections.text: Check the original source[^source]. [^source]: Research notes saved with the manuscript. Check the original source. Research notes saved with the manuscript. Select the small reference number to reach the note at the end of the page. Select its return arrow to go back to the reference. Footnotes remain available on the page that uses them when H2 headings split a chapter into sheets.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Tables and matrices
sections.text: | Format | Result | | --- | --- | | Markdown | Text | | Mermaid | Diagram | [Media examples](./media.md) Format Result Markdown Text Mermaid Diagram Media examples On a narrow page, the table scrolls horizontally while its first column stays visible. Relative chapter links and heading anchors also work.

sections.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
sections.heading: Spell Mode
sections.text: Set magicMode: true in grimoire.yml to show the toggle. Highlights draw across the words, bold text lifts, and strikethrough strokes appear. Effects play once when a page comes into view and respect the device's reduced-motion setting.

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.text: Use Markdown image syntax for still images, animated GIFs, and MP4 files. Resolve local paths from the chapter that uses them. The static build bundles referenced local media.

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: Images and GIFs
sections.text: Use AVIF, WebP, PNG, JPEG, or GIF. Write an alt description inside the brackets. Click or tap an image in the reader to enlarge it. Zoom in to inspect details, choose Fit to see the whole image, or close the viewer to resume reading. ![From Markdown to a static site](../assets/diagram.avif) ![The publishing flow in motion](../assets/publishing-flow.gif) From Markdown to a static site The publishing flow in motion

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: MP4
sections.text: An MP4 renders as a video player inside the page. Playback pauses when you turn away from it. ![Publishing flow video](../assets/publishing-flow.mp4) Publishing flow video

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: YouTube and Vimeo
sections.text: Use the video URL in the same syntax. The embedded player loads when the reader selects it. The source link still works when the video owner restricts embedding. ![YouTube demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M7lc1UVf-VE) ![Vimeo demo](https://vimeo.com/76979871) YouTube demo Vimeo demo

sections.title: Images, video, and diagrams
sections.heading: Mermaid diagrams
sections.text: Set the language of a fenced code block to mermaid. Select the diagram to open the viewer, then zoom and drag to explore. You can also pan with the arrow keys and press Escape to return to the page. flowchart LR subgraph Source Markdown[Markdown chapters] Settings[Project settings] Art[Images and video] end subgraph Build Books[Sort books and chapters] Paper[Split pages at H2] Links[Resolve links and media] end subgraph Output Library[Library] Chapters[Chapter HTML] Sitemap[Sitemap] end Markdown --> Books --> Paper --> Chapters Art --> Links --> Chapters Settings --> Library Settings --> Sitemap Books --> Library
